correctness.rationale: All-order proof reconstructs midpoint keys and proves odd n has no ties; cuts 1 and n−1 are cycles meeting in one point. Their commutators produce all mixed three-cycles, conjugation produces all three-cycles through the common point, and thus the alternating group. Generator parity and the explicit 4t−1 inversion count at cut 2 give the exact subgroup and full S_n. Binomial support, identity, and double stochasticity yield irreducible, aperiodic convergence. Python stdlib exact checker passed 31378 finite tests for n<=63 and exhaustive subgroup closure for n=3,5,7. Infinite theorem rests on written proof, not finite checks.

value.rationale: The introducing 2026 paper singles out odd unglued midpoint interpolation as lacking an upper theorem; absence of midpoint ties makes the issue structurally distinct from even decks. A sharp exact two-cut group classification together with three-cut full support and qualitative ergodicity closes a natural basic reachability question in the same probability model, without claiming an unsupported mixing-time rate. This is a structural statement about an actual stochastic model rather than a generic group lemma alone.
